title: One Point Lesson - Thermal-Shock Avoidance on Start-Up (OPL-EA-5601-04)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-EA-5601-04 - Thermal-Shock Avoidance on Start-Up.

Equipment: EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER), Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 5600 - SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM.

Related Interlock: N/A (control loop only), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-5601.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains thermal-shock avoidance on start-up for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Admitting steam onto a cold tube bundle too fast cracks the tube-to-tubesheet joints, causing internal leaks. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Establish solvent (tube-side) flow first
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Admit steam slowly by ramping the TV-5602 / TIC-5602 set-point
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Warm the exchanger through gradually
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Avoid sudden large steps in the outlet temperature set-point
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Watch for knocking that indicates condensate hammer
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: High tube dP PDT-5605, low solvent outlet temperature | Likely Cause: Hexane fouling / polymer fines deposit on tube bores | Action: Hydrojetted 246 tubes, restored dP and duty, re-gasketed
- Symptom: Hexane weep at channel flange | Likely Cause: Spiral-wound channel gasket relaxed / damaged | Action: Renewed channel gasket, re-torqued in cross pattern
- Symptom: Continuous steam at condensate, high steam use | Likely Cause: Steam trap element failed open | Action: Replaced steam trap element, verified condensate temperature

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Admitting steam onto a cold tube bundle too fast cracks the tube-to-tubesheet joints, causing internal leaks.
- Point 2: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.
- Point 3: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.
